properties.name: Protected-content confidentiality
properties.definition: Unauthorized parties cannot obtain protected-content plaintext within the stated threat model.

properties.name: Protected-content integrity
properties.definition: Unauthorized modification of protected content is detected or rejected within the stated threat model.

properties.name: Message authenticity
properties.definition: A recipient obtains assurance that a protected message was generated by an authorized sender or sender endpoint according to the selected protocol.

properties.name: Peer or endpoint authentication
properties.definition: A participant obtains assurance about the identity or authorization of a communicating peer, device, or endpoint.

properties.name: Authorization integrity
properties.definition: Security-relevant authorization decisions cannot be changed or exercised by an unauthorized principal without detection or rejection within the stated scope.

properties.name: Forward secrecy
properties.definition: Compromise of specified current or long-term secret material does not expose designated past protected content beyond the stated exposure window.

properties.name: Post-compromise security
properties.definition: After a specified compromise ends, protocol evolution can restore one or more stated security properties for later communications.

properties.name: Key or state consistency
properties.definition: Honest participants can prevent or detect materially inconsistent views of cryptographic identity, device, membership, or directory state within the stated model.

properties.name: Downgrade resistance
properties.definition: An adversary cannot cause participants to use a weaker protocol, algorithm, profile, version, or capability than their minimum security policy permits without detection or failure.

properties.name: Replay resistance
properties.definition: Unauthorized replay of previously valid protocol data is rejected or rendered harmless within the stated scope.

properties.name: State rollback resistance
properties.definition: An adversary cannot cause acceptance of security-relevant stale state in a manner that violates the claimed property, or the rollback is detected.

properties.name: Deniability
properties.definition: Protocol evidence is intentionally insufficient, within the defined model, to provide transferable cryptographic proof to an uninvolved third party that a participant authored a communication.

properties.name: Non-repudiation
properties.definition: The system intentionally provides durable attributable evidence such that a defined act can be demonstrated to a third party under the stated model.

properties.name: Metadata minimization
properties.definition: The system reduces collection, retention, disclosure, or linkability of explicitly identified metadata relative to a stated baseline.

properties.name: Metadata confidentiality
properties.definition: Specified metadata is concealed from specified adversaries within the stated threat model.

properties.name: Unlinkability
properties.definition: Specified events, identifiers, messages, or actions cannot be reliably linked to the same principal or relationship by the stated adversary beyond the declared information baseline.

properties.name: Availability
properties.definition: A defined service or operation remains usable under explicitly bounded failure or attack conditions.

properties.name: Recovery confidentiality
properties.definition: Use or compromise of the ordinary recovery mechanism does not disclose protected content beyond the limits explicitly stated by the recovery profile.

properties.name: Backup confidentiality
properties.definition: Stored backup material does not reveal protected content to the specified backup adversary without the required recovery or decryption authority.

properties.name: Software and update integrity
properties.definition: Unauthorized or unapproved modification or substitution of security-relevant software, configuration, or artifacts is prevented or detected within the stated supply-chain model.

properties.name: Build provenance verifiability
properties.definition: A relying party can verify defined provenance information about the production of an artifact, subject to the trust assumptions of the provenance system.

properties.name: Post-quantum confidentiality
properties.definition: Specified protected content remains confidential against the declared post-quantum adversary model.

properties.name: Post-quantum authentication
properties.definition: Specified authentication properties remain valid against the declared active quantum adversary model.
